sources.entry: Lurar - Menu-bar parametric EQ for headphones. Loads the AutoEq catalog and applies it system-wide via Apple's Core Audio Process Tap — no virtual audio driver.

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu-bar parametric EQ for headphones that applies AutoEq presets system-wide through Apple's Core Audio Process Tap, without a virtual audio driver.
summary.what_it_does: Captures audio from every app using a Core Audio Process Tap, runs it through a 10-band vDSP biquad parametric EQ, and sends the result to the selected output device via a raw HAL Audio Unit. It loads the AutoEq headphone catalog (Oratory1990 measurements are mentioned) as built-in presets, and users can add those, fork them into editable presets, or create fully custom ones. Live band editing in an editor window applies to the running engine, with per-device preset recall and a Save/Discard/Delete workflow. Presets are stored as JSON in Application Support and reloaded when the file changes. The README also mentions a loudness offset, crossfeed, a spectrum overlay, and a burn-in tally, plus a release pipeline with signing, notarization, and Sparkle appcast updates.
use_cases: Equalize headphones system-wide on a Mac
Tune a parametric EQ for a specific headphone model
EQ audio without installing a virtual audio driver
Route system audio through a DAC with custom EQ
Per-device EQ preset switching on macOS
notable: No virtual audio driver: taps app audio with Core Audio Process Tap and writes to the DAC through a raw HAL Audio Unit
Loads the AutoEq catalog; built-in presets can be forked with Tweak… and reset to the original curve
Edits apply to the running engine instantly, with the original curve shown as a dashed reference
Per-device preset auto-recall and an auto-detect banner for new output devices
caveats: Requires macOS 14.2 or later (Core Audio Process Tap API)
Apps using HAL hog or exclusive mode cannot be tapped and bypass the EQ
Third-party HAL drivers such as Rogue Amoeba's ARK can cause silence in the EQ'd path
Signed release pipeline needs an Apple Developer ID and several GitHub secrets; the README describes dry runs without signing
